Enhance the AI domain generator of the Nxeon platform at /opt/nxeon and surface it in the customer portal, not just the marketing site.

WHAT EXISTS (read first): app/(marketing)/tools/domain-generator/page.tsx, components/marketing/tools/DomainGeneratorTool.tsx, app/api/tools/domain-generator/route.ts. There is already an AI domain generator on the marketing tools page. Understand exactly what it does now before changing anything.

YOUR FILES (owned exclusively): app/(marketing)/tools/domain-generator/**, components/marketing/tools/DomainGeneratorTool.tsx, app/api/tools/domain-generator/route.ts, and a NEW customer-portal placement (add under app/dashboard/domains/** or a new component in components/customer/ — read how the existing domain search/register components there work: components/customer/DomainSearch.tsx, DomainRegisterWizard.tsx). Plus any new test files.

THE SPIN THE OWNER WANTS:
1. **Describe-your-business input.** The customer types a description of their business plus optional buzzwords/keywords, and the generator produces creative domain ideas from that (via the AI call the tool already uses). Make the input richer than a single keyword — a short business description + a keywords field + optional TLD preferences.
2. **Only surface AVAILABLE domains.** This is the key differentiator. Every suggestion shown must be checked for real availability (the platform already has domain availability checking — find it: lib/registrar.ts / the domain search action / the Namecheap or registrar API used by DomainSearch.tsx) and only genuinely-available ones are presented, ideally with the price to register. Never show a domain as available that is not — if the availability check fails or is uncertain, say "couldn't verify" rather than claim available (this codebase's rule: never report an outcome you did not verify).
3. **Marketing + portal.** Keep/improve the public marketing tool (it is SEO-valuable — this is a high-search-volume tool), AND add it inside the customer portal so a logged-in customer can go idea -> available domain -> register in one flow (wire the portal version into the existing register/purchase path).
4. **SEO.** The marketing page should have strong on-page SEO (title, meta description, H1, descriptive copy, FAQ/schema if the page pattern supports it) since people search for exactly this. Match the existing marketing tools' SEO pattern.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Match the Nxeon design system exactly on both surfaces — read neighbouring components.
- Availability checks and the AI call cost money / hit rate limits; keep the existing rate-limit + `clientIp(await headers())` protection on the public API route (do NOT reintroduce the x-forwarded-for first-hop bug that was just fixed platform-wide — use the shared clientIp helper).
- Do not clone any competitor's copy/branding. Write our own.
- If the AI suggestion call uses Claude, use the correct current model id and message shape — read the existing call, don't guess.

VERIFY: `npx tsc --noEmit` = 0; `npm test` stays green (582) and grows; add tests for the pure logic (suggestion parsing, the available-only filter, "couldn't verify" handling) using stripCommentsAndStrings for any source tripwire. Do NOT build in /opt/nxeon/.next. Do NOT run standalone scripts from a symlinked-node_modules tree (production creds hazard). Do not deploy, restart, or commit — I integrate centrally.

Report: what the tool did before vs after, how availability is verified (and what happens when it can't be), the portal placement + how it hands off to registration, and tests added/proven.

18	 *                       normalised `::ffff:1.2.3.4` and `1.2.3.4:5678` to one
19	 *                       bucket — but hardcoded "one proxy".
20	 *
21	 * Both properties are now in the single `clientIp`, and this is an alias of it.
22	 * Keeping the name costs nothing (about fifteen route handlers import it) and
23	 * deleting the duplicate implementation removes the thing that actually hurts:
24	 * two answers to "who is calling", drifting apart, with no way for a reader to
25	 * know which one their call site should have used. A second definition of an
26	 * existing thing is this codebase's single most common defect class.
27	 *
28	 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
29	 * WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUSTWORTHY (the incident, kept because it is load-bearing)
30	 * ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
31	 * Every route in `app/api/**` used to carry a private copy of:
32	 *
33	 *     const xff = req.headers.get("x-forwarded-for") ?? "";
34	 *     return xff.split(",")[0]?.trim() || "unknown";     // ← FIRST hop
35	 *
36	 * with the comment "first hop of x-forwarded-for is the real client (nginx
37	 * appends downstream)". That comment is backwards, and it made every per-IP rate
38	 * limit on this platform a no-op. All Nxeon vhosts proxy with:
39	 *
40	 *     proxy_set_header X-Real-IP        $remote_addr;
41	 *     proxy_set_header X-Forwarded-For  $proxy_add_x_forwarded_for;
42	 *
43	 * and `$proxy_add_x_forwarded_for` is "the client's X-Forwarded-For header, with
44	 * $remote_addr APPENDED". So a request arriving with `X-Forwarded-For:
45	 * 203.0.113.77` reaches the app as `203.0.113.77, <the real peer>` — leftmost is
46	 * a free-text field the caller filled in.
47	 *
48	 * Verified live against production through nginx on 2026-07-27:
49	 *   curl -H 'X-Forwarded-For: 203.0.113.77' https://nxeon.cloud/api/tools/my-ip
50	 *   → {"ip":"203.0.113.77", "forwardedFor":"203.0.113.77, 127.0.0.1"}
51	 *
52	 * Consequence: rotating one header per request gave an unauthenticated attacker
53	 * an unlimited budget on every throttled endpoint — unbounded row insertion via
54	 * /api/track and /api/chat, unbounded 5 MB blobs via /api/chat/upload, unbounded
55	 * outbound scanning via /api/tools/port-checker, and unbounded spend on the
56	 * platform Claude key and the registrar via /api/tools/domain-generator.
57	 *
58	 * Only values nginx itself writes are trustworthy: `X-Real-IP` (set
59	 * unconditionally, `proxy_set_header` REPLACES any client value) and the LAST
60	 * hop of `X-Forwarded-For` (a client can prepend fake hops; it can never append
61	 * after nginx).

### How availability is verified, and the "couldn't verify" path
Every suggestion is checked through the existing `checkAvailabilityBatched` → `lib/registrar.ts` (`checkDomains`, name.com). The `isRegisterable` guard requires both `status === "available"` and a non-null `priceCents`.
